messages.author: 4b78c958d422dcfc
messages.subject: location of www folder files
parts:
I used the following tutorial to install rApache on Ubuntu 11.04:

http://www.zh-cn.org/en/2011/05/19/english-setting-up-a-rapache-environment/

The tutorial worked great with a couple exceptions. The main problem
is that the configuration file in Step #4 assumes that the www folder
in my home directory has files such as processform.r, helloworld.r,
sendBin.r, and test.R. In order to get the apache server to accept
this configuration, I had to comment out all portions that of this
file that referred to this www folder. I have posted my commented out
configuration file at the end of this post.

I am wondering if the rApache installation puts those files elsewhere
and I need to move these files into a www folder that I create. Or do
I need to download and/or create these files from somewhere else?

Also, I am running into the problem that when I create a "helloworld"
file in my brew folder and combine html code with the brew r-snippets,
the html code does not render but is simply displayed in the browser
as code. In that case, the r-snippets do work. If I then add a .html
extension to the file, the html code will correctly render, but the r-
snippet throws an error. Any ideas?

Thanks in advance for any help somebody could provide on this.
Cheers,
Markus

### rapache configuration file ###


<VirtualHost *:80>
ServerAdmin LJ@localhost
LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
# Place this in the config file to turn error messages into HTML
which
# are printed in the browser. Without this, all warning and error
messages
# are printed to the Apache error log file.
ROutputErrors
DocumentRoot "/home/markus/www"
REvalOnStartup "setwd('/home/markus/www/');suppressWarnings"
<Directory />
Options FollowSymLinks
AllowOverride None
# Order allow,deny
# Allow from all
</Directory>

<Location /RApacheInfo>
SetHandler r-info
</Location>

# <Location /ReadFile>
# SetHandler r-handler
# RFileHandler /home/ilpil/www/processform.r
# </Location>

# <Location /hello>
# SetHandler r-handler
# RFileHandler /home/ilpil/www/helloworld.r
# </Location>

# <Location /sendBin>
# SetHandler r-handler
# RFileHandler /home/ilpil/www/sendBin.r
# </Location>

<Directory /home/markus/www/brew>
SetHandler r-script
RHandler brew::brew
</Directory>

# <Location /R>
# SetHandler r-handler
# RFileHandler /home/ilpil/www/test.R
# </Location>

# <Location /Rblah>
# SetHandler r-handler
# RFileHandler /home/ilpil/www/test.R::main
# </Location>

# <Directory />
# Options FollowSymLinks
# AllowOverride None
# </Directory>

# <Directory /home/ilpil/www/>
# Options Indexes FollowSymLinks MultiViews
# AllowOverride None
# Order allow,deny
# allow from all
# </Directory>

ScriptAlias /cgi-bin/ /usr/lib/cgi-bin/
<Directory "/usr/lib/cgi-bin">
AllowOverride None
Options +ExecCGI -MultiViews +SymLinksIfOwnerMatch
Order allow,deny
Allow from all
</Directory>

ErrorLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/error.log

# Possible values include: debug, info, notice, warn, error, crit,
# alert, emerg.
LogLevel warn

CustomLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/access.log combined

Alias /doc/ "/usr/share/doc/"
<Directory "/usr/share/doc/">
Options Indexes MultiViews FollowSymLinks
AllowOverride None
Order deny,allow
Deny from all
Allow from 127.0.0.0/255.0.0.0 ::1/128
</Directory>
</VirtualHost>

while the I wrote my own processform.r file. The files are under the
test folder of the rapache source code tar ball. You can just simply
comment these part out, and you won't have problem.

try and get this installed and yours finally worked for me.

I am now trying to get your upload file code to work and am running

reading example?" post and am running into a couple problems with the

published the code in the post, you used the directory var/www/images
and in your setup rApache tutorial your directory was /home/ipilar/www
instead. I have my www folder setup in my home folder and tried to
change all the directories to /home/markus/www/images, but that did
not seem to work.

If you could post the processForm.r code, that would have worked with
your installation tutorial along with the html code for uploading a
file, I think that it will work for me. Again, thanks for all your
help on this.
--Markus
